title.credits.description: Who made the game and where NASA's real data and images come from.
credits.title: Credits
credits.subtitle: Hello Mars · a game made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
credits.hint: ↑ ↓ or the mouse wheel to scroll · click a link to open it
credits.ownership: The code, design, writing and final assembly of the game belong to the Hello Mars team. AI tools were used under our direction: we chose, reviewed, edited and integrated everything they generated.
credits.disclaimer: Hello Mars is not an official NASA product and is not endorsed by NASA. NASA data and images are used according to its media usage guidelines:
credits.section.nasaData: NASA data and how the game uses it
credits.game.use: Concept, game design, programming, writing and assembly: Santiago (ship and base simulation) and Facundo (mission flow and maneuvers).
credits.challenge.use: The challenge behind the game: train kids as a crew, with life support, radiation, power and communication decisions based on real data.
credits.donkiFlr.use: Solar flares: the strong flare that announces each 2024 solar storm, and how far in advance the player is warned.
credits.donkiSep.use: Solar particles: the real moment each radiation storm begins, sending the crew to the shelter.
credits.donkiNotices.use: Mission Control messages: strong flares, detected particles and plasma clouds (CMEs) heading to Mars, with their real date.
credits.biosentinel.use: Daily radiation during the trips, and when each 2024 solar storm starts, how high it gets and how long it lasts (real peak: 653 μGy/h).
credits.curiosityRad.use: Daily radiation on the surface of Mars and the real storm of 05/20/2024 at the Gale base (peak: 304 μGy/h).
credits.artemis.use: Crossing the Van Allen belts during launch, with what the Artemis I Orion capsule measured.
credits.tgo.use: Radiation on the trip to Mars in free mode (measured during the 2016 cruise).
credits.rems.use: Daily dust and cold at Gale: how much power the solar panels give, how much heating is needed, and the dust and extreme-night warnings.
credits.radiationDose.use: How harmful radiation is on Mars, in transit and during a storm (quality factor), and NASA's dose limit.
credits.bvad.use: How much oxygen, water and food each crew member uses per day.
credits.std3001.use: The health limits of the meters: carbon dioxide, water per day and per walk outside, calories, water recycling and daily exercise.
credits.osdr.use: The real science facts about radiation and plants shown when completing missions.
credits.conjunctions.use: Solar conjunction: the days when the Sun sits between Earth and Mars and there is no contact with Mission Control.
credits.planets.use: Where Earth and Mars are each day: how long Mission Control's signal takes to arrive (seconds at departure, about 20 minutes at Mars).
credits.galeFacts.use: The real figures and names of Gale Crater shown on Mars: its size, Mount Sharp, Gediz Vallis, pure sulfur and the dunes.
credits.blueMarble.use: The Earth spinning on the main menu, reduced to 20 colors.
credits.vikingMdim.use: Mars spinning on the main menu, reduced to 12 colors.
credits.galeCrater.use: The Gale Crater map with Curiosity's route (V key on Mars).
credits.galePhotos.use: Photos from Curiosity and the MRO orbiter used as reference to draw each area outside the Gale base (not shown in the game).
credits.devin.use: Coding assistant: helped write the code, tools and documentation, always directed and reviewed by the team.
credits.lyria.use: Soundtrack generation: the 12 tracks, one for each moment of the mission, later mastered by the team.
credits.elevenlabs.use: Sound effect and ambience generation: doors, alarms, minigames, engines, footsteps and more.
credits.openaiImage.use: Base image generation: crew, ship, base, objects, icons, logo and launch scenery.
credits.pixelSnapper.use: Snaps the generated images to a grid of real pixels and a limited palette, so they become true pixel art.
credits.phaser.use: The game engine: rendering, animation, keyboard and mouse, and scenes.
credits.typescript.use: The language the game is written in.
credits.tiled.use: Editor for the ship and Gale base maps.
credits.ffmpeg.use: Music mastering: even loudness, limiter and loop points.
